newsitem.title: BURUNDI: Burundi party leader arrested and jailed.
newsitem.headline: Burundi party leader arrested and jailed.

text.p: The secretary general of the Frodebu political party which ran Burundi up until a military coup last July was arrested on Tuesday and taken to prison, prison officials and his wife said.

The wife of Augustin Nzogibwani said police had given her a statement which accused him of distributing anti-government tracts, inciting civil war and making false statements which could create panic.
"As a result he has sabotaged government efforts to re-establish peace," the statement said according to Schola Nzogibwani.
Burundi's countryside is gripped by a vicious war between the mainly-Tutsi army and militias of the majority Hutu ethnic group, which has killed at least 150,000 people since 1993.

Nzogibwani, who was put under house arrest on Sunday, recently described a new army tactic of grouping Hutu peasants in camps away from their villages, officially for their own protection, as equivalent to setting up concentration camps.

Frodebu, mainly backed by Hutus, won the country's first multi-party elections in 1993, and was part of a power-sharing agreement until Major Pierre Buyoya, a Tutsi, took over in a military coup last July.
Other countries in the region have imposed economic sanctions on Burundi to force a swift restoration of democracy.
